title: Minimal commitment anchor experiments
content:
Quick back-of-envelope experiments for a minimum-commitment starter tier (notes to self).

Goal: design a low-friction entry tier that signals value via small monetary commit (card on file / $X/mo) but still gives meaningful volume of inference so new users integrate and build habit.

Assumptions (rough):
- Avg model mix: 60% embeddings (short, batched), 30% chat (medium tokens), 10% llm-heavy (long generation).
- Token mix avg per active session: 1. Input 120 tokens, output 420 tokens => ~540 tokens per interaction.
- Sessions per active user per day: 6 (conservative product hypothesis).
- Active days per month per new user cohort: 12 (early-stage retention).

Compute and cost primitives: (very rough, replace with infra numbers)
- GPU hour effective cost (amortized infra + infra ops): $2.40 / GPU-hour for shared fleet (hosted).
- Throughput: small-chat model ~120 tokens/sec on average on serving runtime per slot.
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour ≈ 120 * 3600 = 432k tokens/hr.
- Cost per token ≈ $2.40 / 432k ≈ $0.0000056 per token (5.6e-6).
  - Note: this is naive; embeddings and batching shift this down. Embeddings batched -> effective < $1.0e-6/token for that portion.

Back-of-envelope: 
- Monthly tokens consumed by one starter user: 540 tokens/session * 6 sess/day * 12 days = 38,880 tokens/month ≈ 39k.
- Cost to Redwood (naive average) ≈ 39k * $0.0000056 ≈ $0.22 per month per active starter user.
- Add infra margin + storage + control plane + support ops (x3 multiplier) => full cost ≈ $0.66.

Pricing anchors (experiments):
A) $5/month card-on-file -> includes 100k tokens + 30k embeddings units (or whatever metric)
  - If avg usage = 39k tokens, Redwood margin ~ $4.34 -> covers CAC subsidy for short period.
  - Upsell levers: extra tokens at payg, seat + feature gates, webhook priority.

B) $1/month min-commit + credits: 2,000 free tokens + 50% off first 100k overage for 3 months.
  - Intent: remove plastic friction but require micro-commit to keep churn honest.
  - Risk: subsidy too large if usage spikes. Need per-customer caps.

C) $20/year (annual micro-commit) with 250k token bucket, non-rollover. 
  - Easier for SMB sign-up (small commitment), unit math: $20/year vs cost @ $0.66/mo => $7.92/year cost -> gross margin good for long tail.

Sessionization + credit decay idea:
- Convert token budget to session credits for UX simplicity: e.g., 7 credits = 1 premium convo (540 tokens). 
- Credit decay: credits replenish weekly, not monthly, to spread usage and reduce burst risk.
- Rationale: easier to explain to non-technical buyers and reduces instantaneous load spikes.

Burst protection / guardrails (operational thoughts):
- Soft throttle after 2x expected velocity; hard cap at 10x monthly tokens (blocks further generation until refill or upgrade).
- Auto-detect embedding-heavy workloads and route to cheaper embedding pools; bill differently (embedding units).

Commitment economics sketch (for Dedicated conversion funnel):
- If baseline starter converts to Dedicated (monthly reserved) @ $Xk/month, need to forecast: 
  - Lifetime from starter to committed = 6 months median (hypothesis).
  - Required conversion rate to Dedicated to make starter subsidy payback: subsidy_per_user / (ARR_per_converted_customer * conversion_rate).
  - Example numbers: subsidy = $15 (first 3 months), ARR contribution per converted customer = $12k/yr -> at 1% conversion, payback too slow. Need higher conversion or lower subsidy.

Pricing lever matrix (things to A/B):
- Anchor price (mental): $1 vs $5 vs $10 monthly.
- Included token quantity: 5k / 25k / 100k.
- Commitment visibility: auto-renew vs opt-in annual.
- Activation reward: extra credits for first 7 days vs monotonic weekly drip.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate infra cost-per-token with infra econ (ask Jin) — current numbers are placeholders.
- Simulate cohort flows: create Monte Carlo for variable retention (d0, d7, d30) and compute break-even for subsidies at different conversion rates. (Linked: Linear PRICING-412).
- UX experiments: which framing reduces churn? ("$5/mo for 100k tokens" vs "7 premium conversations per week") Need two copytests.
- Legal/check: are free-tier card-on-file experiments okay? Compliance to payments and auto-charge rules. @Miguel to confirm.

Notes-to-self on metric naming:
- Active_starter_user = user who consumes > 1 conversation in 7 days.
- Token_velocity = tokens / active_day (median across cohort).
- Effective_cost_per_token = infrastructure + ops + amortized CAC / expected lifetime tokens.

Edge-case heuristics:
- Bots / scraping detection: if > 70% requests are identical patterns or high rps from single API key, throttle to payg and warn.
- Partner bundles: allow marketplace partners to offer starter at discount but require attribution so conversion is trackable.

Short experiment roadmap (3 sprints):
1) Build simulator + sanity-check infra token cost (sprint 1).
2) Launch two lightweight price/copy A/Bs in the webflow for organic signups (sprint 2).
3) Monitor conversion to paid tiers and SLO violations; tune caps and drip cadence (sprint 3).

Random scribbles: 
- Could we offer "1 free premium convo per day" forever and then charge payg? Simpler mental model than tokens. But gaming risk.
- Consider embedding quotas separately (per-embedding-unit) to avoid cross-subsidy from expensive embedding traffic.

End of notes.

Unresolved: what to show in billing UI: tokens left vs conversations left? (both?)

-- A.P.
